html:
The Costa Rican Civil War was a six-week war in March and April 1948, set off when Congress annulled a presidential election won by the opposition candidate, Otilio Ulate. About two thousand people died.

The government of Teodoro Picado was allied with the former president Rafael Ángel Calderón Guardia, the Church and the communists, who had together built the country's social laws. Its opponents, led by the farmer José Figueres, rose from the southern hills with help from abroad and won.

A junta under Figueres ruled for eighteen months. It kept the social laws, nationalised the banks, gave women the vote, and abolished the army. The war was the last in Costa Rica, which has since been one of the most stable democracies in the Americas.
sum: The Costa Rican Civil War was a six-week war in March and April 1948, set off when Congress annulled a presidential election won by the opposition candidate, Otilio Ulate. About two thousand people died.
